stack.Face: Any image generator that keeps a character consistent from a reference
stack.Motion: Veo 3.1, Kling 3.0, Hailuo 2.3, Seedance 2.0, or Runway Gen-4.5. Pick one and check its free tier today
stack.Voice: Your own voice. If you use text-to-speech, use one whose licence allows monetised videos

talking.lasts: A compilation of random babies gets one spike. A named pair can become a series.
steps: Save two faces. Give them names and do not change them.
Write three exchanges. The third one is the joke. Cut anything before that.
Record both voices yourself, different pitch, same mic.
Cut on each line. Do not hold a face while the other talks.
Caption the names once, then the lines.
Turn on the synthetic-content label. Next episode is the same pair in the same place.
talking.shape:
A asks for one thing.
B gives the wrong thing, twice.
A gets angry.
B's last line shows A was saying the helper's name, not the thing.

prompts.label: 1. Script prompt
prompts.text:
Write [3] short scripts for two original AI baby characters. [NAME A] is [trait, e.g. bossy]. [NAME B] is [trait, e.g. clueless]. Setting: [ROOM].

Each script has three exchanges. The third exchange is the joke and must reverse what the first exchange set up. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English]. At most 12 words per line. No real people, no brands.

Output: a table with speaker, line, on-screen caption.

prompts.label: 2. Character sheet prompt
prompts.text: Two original fictional babies side by side, about one year old, each with a different hair and outfit. Baby A: [DESCRIPTION]. Baby B: [DESCRIPTION]. Front view, plain light background, soft studio light, same faces every time, no text, no logo. Soft 3D animation look. Invented characters, not real children.

prompts.label: 3. Scene prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool, with the character sheet attached
prompts.text: Locked-off two-shot in [ROOM]. Baby A on the left, Baby B on the right, both facing camera. Baby A says: "[LINE]". Baby B turns, then says: "[LINE]". Lips match speech. Soft daylight, no camera shake, 8 seconds. Keep both faces identical to the reference image.

talking.avoid: A new pair every upload, or a real child's photo as either face.

horror.lasts: A one-off jump scare dies fast. A numbered series is what viewers follow.
steps: Put the episode number on screen from the first second.
Write a normal first line. Someone is home, or having tea, or on a call.
Add one detail that is wrong. Do not explain it in the middle.
Use three stills. Cut when the sentence changes, not on a timer.
Keep one narrator voice for the whole series.
End on the line that reframes the start. Stop. Turn on the synthetic-content label.
horror.shape: Episode 4. She is drinking tea. The clock says 1:30. The last line is about who poured it.

prompts.label: 1. Script prompt
prompts.text:
Write episode [NUMBER] of an original horror series. Narrator: first person, calm. About 80 words.

Structure: a normal first line in an ordinary place ([PLACE]). One detail that is wrong, stated plainly. No explanation. A last line that changes what the first line meant.

No gore, no real people, no real places. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English].

Also output three still-image descriptions, one per sentence group, and one line for the on-screen episode title.

prompts.label: 2. Still prompt
prompts.text: Vertical 9:16 still. [PLACE] at night, one warm lamp, deep shadows, a small detail that is slightly wrong: [WRONG DETAIL]. No visible faces, no text, no gore. Cinematic, muted colours, film grain.

prompts.label: 3. Motion prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool, with the still attached
prompts.text: Slow push-in on this still for 6 seconds. Very small movement: a curtain shifts, a light flickers once. No people appear. Keep the composition identical. No sudden cuts.

horror.avoid: Gore close-ups, a new narrator every episode, and explaining the twist after it lands.

myth.lasts: One myth clip can spike. One art style lasts longer than a new god every upload.
steps: Pick one event. Not the whole epic.
Open on the conflict in the first two seconds. Skip the family tree.
Lock one art style and reuse it. A new look every week is a new channel.
Write the voiceover first, then make stills that match the lines.
Caption every line. Keep music under the voice.
Turn on the synthetic-content label. The next episode is the next event, same style.
myth.shape: Line 1 names the fight. Line 2 is the choice. Line 3 is the consequence. Stop.

prompts.label: 1. Script prompt
prompts.text:
Retell one event from [STORY, e.g. the Mahabharata]: [EVENT]. About 70 words, for a vertical video.

Line 1 names the conflict. Line 2 shows the choice. Line 3 shows the consequence. No family tree, no intro. Respectful tone. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English].

Also output four shot descriptions in one consistent art style: [STYLE, e.g. painted miniature, warm colours].

prompts.label: 2. Style prompt
prompts.text: Vertical 9:16 illustration in [STYLE]. Scene: [SHOT DESCRIPTION]. Same palette and brush style as the rest of the series. Dramatic lighting, no text, no modern objects.

prompts.label: 3. Motion prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool, with the illustration attached
prompts.text: Animate this illustration for 6 seconds: slow camera push, drifting dust or smoke, a cloth moving in wind. Characters do not change shape. Keep the painted style.

myth.avoid: Five scenes in 15 seconds, or a different painter every episode.

dance.lasts: The sound peaks in a few days. The character can outlast the sound.
steps: Use a dance clip you have the rights to. One person, full body.
Make a character. Do not use a living person's photo, and do not use a celebrity.
Put the still onto the dance with a motion tool. Export vertical.
Keep the face sharp. If the hands melt, redo that take.
Same character next time. Change the sound only to one you can use.
Turn on the synthetic-content label.
dance.shape: No dialogue. The first frame is the character already moving. A caption names them.

prompts.label: 1. Character prompt
prompts.text: Full-body original character for a dance video: [DESCRIPTION, e.g. a cheerful mango with arms and legs]. Standing pose, arms slightly away from the body, plain background, even light, clear hands and feet, no text. Soft 3D animation look. Invented character.

prompts.label: 2. Motion prompt
prompts.tool: A motion-transfer tool such as Viggle, or a video model with a driving clip
prompts.text: Apply the movement of the attached dance clip to the character in the attached image. Keep the character's shape, colours, and face identical. Full body in frame, no cropping, no extra people.

prompts.label: 3. Caption prompt
prompts.text: Write five caption options for a short dance video of an original character named [NAME]. Each at most six words, playful, no hashtags, no real people.

dance.avoid: A private person's face, or a celebrity's face, on the dance.

objects.lasts: The object is the series. A new object every day resets the channel.
steps: Pick one object and give it a face you can redraw.
One action only: dancing, cooking, or answering a phone.
Keep the object readable. If it turns into a person, you lost the joke.
Add one caption. Do not narrate a plot.
Turn on the synthetic-content label.
Next video is the same object in a new room, or the same action with a second object.
objects.shape: Frame 1: the object is already in the action. Caption: what they think they are doing.

prompts.label: 1. Idea prompt
prompts.text: My channel is about one original object character: [OBJECT, e.g. a talking brinjal]. Give me 15 one-action video ideas. Each is one human action the object tries, plus a six-word caption. Keep every idea possible in one 8-second shot.

prompts.label: 2. Character prompt
prompts.text: An original character: [OBJECT] with a simple face, two small arms, and two legs. Centred, plain background, soft light, bold clear shapes, no text. Pixar-like 3D look. Keep the object's shape recognisable.

prompts.label: 3. Scene prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool, with the character attached
prompts.text: The character [ACTION] in [ROOM]. Static camera, 8 seconds. The character keeps its exact shape and face. Natural, slightly clumsy movement. No text.

objects.avoid: A real pet's owner footage passed off as yours, or a new mascot every upload.

love.lasts: A single kiss clip is one post. A couple with names can be a serial.
steps: Name both people and save their faces. Original adults. Not a real couple.
Write five lines: meeting, a promise, a doubt, a proof, a turn.
Show the promise on screen as text, so the turn can break it.
Use the same clothes and the same street so it feels like one story.
Caption the dialogue. Music stays under the lines.
Turn on the synthetic-content label. Episode 2 starts from the turn, not from a new couple.
love.shape: They meet. He promises one thing. She finds the opposite. The last line is his, and it is not an apology.

prompts.label: 1. Script prompt
prompts.text: Write a 5-line love story for two original adult characters, [NAME A] and [NAME B], set in [PLACE]. Lines: meeting, a promise, a doubt, a proof, a turn that reverses the promise. At most 14 words per line. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English]. No real people. Output: speaker, line, caption, shot note.

prompts.label: 2. Cast prompt
prompts.text: Two original adult characters for a romance short. [NAME A]: [DESCRIPTION]. [NAME B]: [DESCRIPTION]. Front and three-quarter view of each, plain background, soft light, consistent faces and outfits, no text. Invented people, not based on anyone real.

prompts.label: 3. Scene prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool, with the cast attached
prompts.text: Medium shot, [STREET OR ROOM], golden-hour light. [NAME A] says: "[LINE]". [NAME B] looks away, then answers: "[LINE]". Natural expressions, slow camera drift, 8 seconds. Faces identical to the reference.

love.avoid: A real person's face as either lead, or a new couple every video.

guess.lasts: The format stays. Each clip is used once.
steps: Pick two clips of the same kind of shot: a face, a street, or an animal.
One must be generated by you. The other must be footage you can use.
Ask the question in the first second, in text, before either clip plays.
Hold each clip long enough to see one flaw or one real detail.
Reveal the answer in the last two seconds. Do not talk over the reveal.
Label the generated clip as AI in the caption and turn on the synthetic-content label.
guess.shape: Text: which one is AI? Clip A. Clip B. Text: B. One frozen frame of the tell.

prompts.label: 1. Generation prompt
prompts.text: [SUBJECT, e.g. a street vendor handing over a cup of tea]. Handheld phone-camera look, natural light, 6 seconds, ordinary framing, no cinematic grading. It should look like a clip someone filmed on a phone.

prompts.label: 2. Matching prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool or your own camera
prompts.text: Film or source one real clip of the same subject and framing: [SUBJECT]. Same length, same time of day. Use only footage you own or have the licence to use.

prompts.label: 3. Reveal caption prompt
prompts.text: Write ten opening questions for a Real-or-AI video, each at most seven words, curious not clickbait, and five reveal lines that name one visible tell (hands, text, reflections, shadows).

guess.avoid: Using someone else's viral clip as the 'real' half without the right to use it.

talker.lasts: The character is the channel. A new face every week does not stick.
steps: Design one adult character. Do not copy a creator's face.
Write one opinion in four lines. The first line is the claim, not a hello.
Record it in your own voice, or use on-screen text if you will not use a cloned voice.
Same background, same clothes, same framing every time.
Caption the claim in the first second.
Turn on the synthetic-content label. The next video is a new opinion, same person.
talker.shape: Line 1: the claim. Line 2: the example. Line 3: the mistake people make. Line 4: the claim again, shorter.

prompts.label: 1. Script prompt
prompts.text: Write [5] four-line talking-head scripts for an original adult AI character named [NAME] who gives [TOPIC, e.g. study advice] opinions. Line 1 is the claim. Line 2 is an example. Line 3 is the mistake people make. Line 4 repeats the claim, shorter. At most 14 words a line. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English].

prompts.label: 2. Character prompt
prompts.text: Original adult character, [AGE RANGE], [LOOK], plain [COLOUR] background, centred, shoulders up, looking at the camera, neutral expression, soft front light. Not based on any real person or creator. No text.

prompts.label: 3. Talking-clip prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool or talking-photo tool
prompts.text: The character speaks to camera: "[LINE]". Natural blinking, small head movements, lips match the audio. Static framing, no zoom, 8 seconds. Keep the face identical to the reference.

talker.avoid: A real creator's face, a minor's likeness, or a different character every upload.

serial.lasts: Episode 1 can be small. The series is the product if the cliffhanger is real.
steps: Write the season in ten episodes before you generate anything.
Lock the cast. Same mother, same house, same neighbour.
Episode 1 starts in the problem. No intro card longer than a second.
End on a line that episode 2 has to answer. Put the episode number on screen.
Caption in the language you speak. Keep the voice clear of music.
Turn on the synthetic-content label. Upload the next episode while the first is still being shared.
serial.shape: She comes home. One thing is missing. She asks who took it. Cut before the answer.

prompts.label: 1. Season prompt
prompts.text: Plan a 10-episode family drama for an original cast: [CAST, e.g. mother, son, neighbour]. Setting: [PLACE]. Give a one-line premise, then ten episodes. Each episode: one sentence of plot, and one last line that episode N+1 must answer. Language of dialogue: [Hinglish / Hindi / English]. No real people.

prompts.label: 2. Episode prompt
prompts.text: Using the plan above, write episode [N] as a vertical-video script of about 90 words. Open inside the problem. Include speaker, line, caption, and shot note. End on the cliffhanger line.

prompts.label: 3. Scene prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool, with the cast attached
prompts.text: [SHOT, e.g. the mother stands in the doorway holding an empty plate]. Keep both characters identical to the reference. Indoor warm light, slow camera drift, 8 seconds. She says: "[LINE]". Lips match speech.

serial.avoid: A full movie in one video, or a new cast in episode 2.

film.lasts: Each film stands alone. The style of the turn is what people come back for.
steps: Write the last line first. Then write only the setup that line needs.
Three shots: the normal world, the choice, the turn.
Say the character's name in the first line.
No second twist. If you have one, cut it.
Hold the last frame for a beat with the line on screen.
Turn on the synthetic-content label.
film.shape: Ayesha takes one bite. She thinks it fixed the day. The last line says what the bite actually was.

prompts.label: 1. Twist prompt
prompts.text: Give me 10 one-twist story ideas for a 60-second vertical short. For each: the last line, then the three shots that set it up (normal world, choice, turn). Original characters only. Tone: [TONE]. No real people.

prompts.label: 2. Script prompt
prompts.text: Write idea number [N] as a script of about 100 words. Name the character in the first line. Output speaker, line, caption, shot note. The last line must change the meaning of the first shot.

prompts.label: 3. Shot prompt
prompts.text: [SHOT]. Cinematic, shallow depth of field, one lead character who keeps an identical face across shots, 8 seconds, slow camera move. No text on screen.

film.avoid: A moral spoken after the twist, or a cast the viewer meets in the last second.

faith.lasts: A single verse clip spikes. A scene told in the same art style can continue.
steps: Pick one scene you can tell in four lines. Not a whole scripture.
Use an illustrated style, not a real preacher's face or voice.
Put the scene's name on screen in the first second.
Read it in your own voice. Do not clone a reciter.
Caption every line.
Turn on the synthetic-content label and say AI in the caption, so it is not mistaken for a recording of a person.
faith.shape: Title of the scene. What was asked. What was done. The line people repeat.

prompts.label: 1. Script prompt
prompts.text: Retell this story respectfully in four short lines, for a vertical video: [STORY]. Use plain language. Do not invent dialogue and do not add details that are not in the traditional account. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English]. Then list the scene's key image.

prompts.label: 2. Illustration prompt
prompts.text: Vertical 9:16 illustration of [SCENE], in a flat, painterly style. Faces of sacred figures are not shown or are shown only as light. Calm palette, no text, no modern objects.

prompts.label: 3. Motion prompt
prompts.text: Animate this illustration for 6 seconds with slow drifting light and a gentle camera push. No face animation. Keep the style.

faith.avoid: A real scholar's face, a cloned recitation, or presenting the clip as filmed history.

wedding.lasts: One wedding is one post. A family, across episodes, is a serial.
steps: Start in the middle of the argument. Skip the baraat and the invitations.
Two people only. A third person can appear in the last line, not before.
The fight is about one object or one guest. Not about the whole marriage.
Keep the same outfits if this is episode 2 of a family.
End on a line the other person does not answer.
Turn on the synthetic-content label.
wedding.shape: She asks where he was. He answers a different hour. She repeats the question. He names someone else.

prompts.label: 1. Script prompt
prompts.text: Write a 6-line argument between two original characters, [NAME A] and [NAME B], at a wedding. The argument is about one object: [OBJECT]. Start in the middle. At most 12 words a line. The last line is a line the other person cannot answer. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English]. No real people.

prompts.label: 2. Cast prompt
prompts.text: Two original adult characters in Indian wedding clothes. [NAME A]: [DESCRIPTION]. [NAME B]: [DESCRIPTION]. Front and three-quarter view of each, plain background, consistent faces, no text. Invented people.

prompts.label: 3. Scene prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool, with the cast attached
prompts.text: Medium two-shot, a wedding hall corridor, warm light. [NAME A] says: "[LINE]". [NAME B] answers: "[LINE]". Natural gestures, static camera, 8 seconds, identical faces and outfits to the reference.

wedding.avoid: A real couple's photos, or a five-minute family tree before the fight.

story.label: Story and comedy episode
steps: Write the last line before anything else.
Cut every line that does not set up the last line.
Fix one cast and one place. Reuse them every episode.
Make one reference image per character and attach it to every clip.
Caption every spoken line. Keep music under the voice.
Turn on the synthetic-content label and change the joke, not the cast, in the next episode.

prompts.label: 1. Script prompt
prompts.text: Write a [LENGTH] vertical-video script about [NICHE]. Original characters only. Start inside the problem. One twist. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English]. Output a table with speaker, line, caption, and a shot note of at most six words. Last line must change the meaning of the first.

prompts.label: 2. Cast prompt
prompts.text: Character sheet for an original [NICHE] series: [DESCRIPTION]. Front and three-quarter view, plain background, consistent face and outfit, no text. Invented characters.

prompts.label: 3. Scene prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool, with the cast attached
prompts.text: [SHOT]. Keep every face identical to the reference. Soft light, slow camera, [8] seconds, no text on screen.

story.avoid: Real people's faces, a new cast every upload, and a story that explains its own twist.

explainer.label: Voice-over explainer
steps: Pick one question a viewer would type into search.
Write the answer in 6 to 8 short paragraphs. Open with the answer, then give the proof.
Check every number against a source you can name. Put the source in the description.
Record the voice yourself, or use text-to-speech whose licence allows monetised videos.
Lay visuals under each paragraph: maps, charts, stock footage you can use, or AI stills.
Turn on the synthetic-content label if the visuals are generated. Add your own point of view so it is not a template.

prompts.label: 1. Research prompt
prompts.tool: ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude, with web access on
prompts.text: I am making a video about [TOPIC]. List the 8 most important facts, each with a dated source I can open. Mark any fact you are not sure about. Do not invent numbers.

prompts.label: 2. Script prompt
prompts.text: Using only the facts above, write a [LENGTH] voice-over script about [TOPIC] for [AUDIENCE]. Open with the answer in one sentence. One idea per paragraph. After each paragraph, add a bracket with a visual: a map, chart, footage type, or still. Plain words. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English].

prompts.label: 3. Visual prompt
prompts.text: Vertical 9:16 [chart / map / still] showing [VISUAL FROM THE SCRIPT]. Clean, flat colours, readable labels, no invented numbers, no logos.

explainer.avoid: Numbers you cannot source, a narrator that reads a Wikipedia page word for word, and one template for every video.

news.label: Weekly news and tools
steps: Pick the three items that changed this week. Skip anything that did not.
Open each item on the official page and read the date.
Write one line on what it changes for the viewer.
Record yourself or use on-screen text over screen captures.
Post once a week at the same time.
Pin a comment with the links.

prompts.label: 1. Digest prompt
prompts.tool: ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude, with web access on
prompts.text: List the three biggest changes this week in [TOPIC]. For each give the date, one sentence on what changed, and the official link. Say if you cannot confirm something.

prompts.label: 2. Script prompt
prompts.text: Turn the three items into a [LENGTH] script. For each: what changed, who it matters to, one thing to do about it. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English]. No hype words.

prompts.label: 3. Title prompt
prompts.text: Give me 10 titles under 60 characters for this video. Each must name a specific thing that changed, with no clickbait.

news.avoid: Reposting a press release as your own opinion, and claims you could not confirm.

tutorial.label: Screen tutorial
steps: Choose one job a person is trying to finish today.
Do the job once yourself, off camera, and note where you got stuck.
Record your screen at 1080p with the cursor visible.
Open with the finished result in the first five seconds.
Speak each step in one sentence. Cut dead air.
Put the file or template in the description.

prompts.label: 1. Outline prompt
prompts.text: I am recording a screen tutorial on [TASK] using [TOOL]. List the steps in order, with the one mistake beginners make at each step and the keystroke or menu path.

prompts.label: 2. Script prompt
prompts.text: Write the voice-over for a [LENGTH] tutorial from those steps. Start by showing the finished result. One sentence per step. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English].

prompts.label: 3. Description prompt
prompts.text: Write a video description with a timestamp for every step, the tool versions I used, and a one-line summary.

tutorial.avoid: A tool that has changed since you recorded. Check the version before you post.

listicle.label: Review or ranked list
steps: Pick five items a viewer is actually choosing between.
Decide the test before you rank: price, durability, or speed.
Show each item on screen for the same amount of time.
Say the one flaw first, then the one strength.
Rank at the end and say why in one sentence.
Put prices and where you checked them in the description.

prompts.label: 1. Criteria prompt
prompts.text: I am reviewing [PRODUCT TYPE] for [AUDIENCE]. Give me five criteria a buyer should test, with how to test each in under a minute on camera.

prompts.label: 2. Script prompt
prompts.text: Write a [LENGTH] ranked script for these [N] items: [ITEMS]. For each: the one flaw first, then the one strength, then a score out of 10 on [CRITERION]. End with the ranking and one reason. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English]. No invented specs.

prompts.label: 3. B-roll prompt
prompts.text: Vertical 9:16 product shot of [ITEM] on a plain surface, soft side light, slow rotation, no brand text added. Use only for items you do not own and say in the video that it is an illustration.

listicle.avoid: Specs you did not check, and a ranking you did not test.

animation.label: Stick-figure or whiteboard animation
steps: Pick one idea that fits on one drawing.
Write the script in short lines, one idea per line.
Draw one stick figure and fix its look.
Generate or draw one frame per line and keep the style the same.
Animate with simple moves: pan, pop-in, draw-on.
Add captions and a voice. Turn on the synthetic-content label if the frames are generated.

prompts.label: 1. Script prompt
prompts.text: Write a [LENGTH] script that explains [IDEA] with a stick figure. One idea per line, at most 12 words. After each line give a frame description of one stick-figure drawing. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English].

prompts.label: 2. Frame prompt
prompts.text: Hand-drawn black marker stick figure on a white background, simple line art, no shading, no text except [LABEL]. Scene: [FRAME DESCRIPTION]. Same figure and line weight as the other frames. Vertical 9:16.

prompts.label: 3. Motion prompt
prompts.text: Animate with a slow pan and a draw-on reveal. Keep the line drawing flat. 3 seconds per frame.

animation.avoid: A different drawing style on every frame.

satisfying.label: Satisfying loop
steps: Pick one material and one action: soap and a knife, sand and a mould.
Light it from one side and lock the camera.
Record a clean take with no talking.
Cut on the sound. Silence is part of the video.
Loop the last frame into the first.
Post the same action with a new material.

prompts.label: 1. Idea prompt
prompts.text: Give me 20 satisfying-video ideas that use [MATERIAL] and one repeated action, each shootable in a single locked shot at home. Note the sound each one makes.

prompts.label: 2. Shot prompt
prompts.tool: Your video tool, if you generate instead of film
prompts.text: Macro shot of [ACTION on MATERIAL], locked camera, soft side light, clean background, slow and precise movement, real material physics, 8 seconds, seamless loop.

prompts.label: 3. Caption prompt
prompts.text: Write 10 captions of at most five words for a satisfying video of [ACTION on MATERIAL]. No hashtags.

satisfying.avoid: Generated physics that look wrong. Viewers notice.

handson.label: Hands-on how-to
steps: Pick one job that finishes in under a minute on camera.
Film top-down or hands-only with the camera locked.
Say the result in the first line.
Show every step once, then the result.
Add measurements and times as text.
Post the same job with a new variation.

prompts.label: 1. Outline prompt
prompts.text: I am filming a hands-only video on [JOB]. List the steps, the quantities or times, and the mistake people make at each step. Keep it under 60 seconds.

prompts.label: 2. Script prompt
prompts.text: Write on-screen text and a 40-word voice-over for the steps above. Open with the result. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English].

prompts.label: 3. Title prompt
prompts.text: Give me 10 titles under 55 characters for this how-to. Name the result, not the process.

handson.avoid: Health or safety advice you cannot back up. State what you used and what you did not check.

commentary.label: Breakdown or commentary
steps: Use footage you own or have the licence to use. Do not rip clips.
Pick one moment and pause on it.
Say what happened in one sentence.
Draw or point to the detail that matters.
Give your own take. That is what makes it yours.
End with what you would do differently.

prompts.label: 1. Breakdown prompt
prompts.text: I am doing a breakdown of [MOMENT] in [SPORT OR GAME]. List what happened in order, the one decision that mattered, and the detail a casual viewer misses.

prompts.label: 2. Script prompt
prompts.text: Write a [LENGTH] voice-over for that breakdown. First line: what happened. Then the detail. Then my opinion: [OPINION]. Language: [Hinglish / Hindi / English].

prompts.label: 3. Graphic prompt
prompts.text: A clean top-down diagram of [SITUATION] with arrows showing [MOVEMENT]. Flat colours, no logos, no real player faces.

commentary.avoid: Ripped clips from broadcasters, and real players' faces in generated frames.

quote.label: Quote and affirmation video
steps: Pick a quote that is in the public domain, or write your own.
Choose one image style and keep it.
Show one line at a time with the voice.
Keep the music quiet.
End on the quote on screen for two seconds.
Post at the same hour each day.

prompts.label: 1. Writing prompt
prompts.text: Write 20 short original lines about [THEME] in the voice of a calm teacher. At most 15 words each. No quotes from living authors.

prompts.label: 2. Image prompt
prompts.text: Vertical 9:16 background in [STYLE, e.g. misty mountains at dawn], plenty of empty space at the top for text, calm colours, no text, no people.

prompts.label: 3. Motion prompt
prompts.text: Slow parallax drift over this image for 8 seconds. Mist moves slightly. Keep the empty space clear.

quote.avoid: Quotes from living authors, and invented quotes with a famous name attached.

ambient.label: Ambient or long loop
steps: Pick one sound or one scene.
Make or source audio you have the licence to use.
Loop a slow visual. Nothing flashes.
Make the video one to three hours long.
Put the sleep or study use in the title.
Check licences before you post.

prompts.label: 1. Scene prompt
prompts.text: A calm [SCENE, e.g. rain on a window at night] in a 10-second seamless loop, slow movement, no people, no text, soft light.

prompts.label: 2. Sound brief
prompts.text: [SOUND, e.g. soft steady rain], no music, no sudden sounds, even volume, seamless loop.

prompts.label: 3. Title prompt
prompts.text: Give me 10 titles under 60 characters for a [DURATION] video of [SOUND] for [USE: sleep or study].

ambient.avoid: Copyrighted music, and loops with a visible jump.
